metadata.author: hand-authored, Docs/11_phase2_semantic_analysis.md M5
metadata.granularity: module + class + top-level function anchors only (no methods) -- score.py normalizes every anchor to its top-level defining symbol before comparing, so a predicted set citing methods is not penalized for going one level deeper than this file does
metadata.disclosure: Authored with prior awareness of one specific Claude Code investigation's own component breakdown (inspected during M1/M2 development) -- not a fully blind gold set. Groupings below deliberately differ from that run's in several places (Data Structures split from Form Parsing; Concurrency Utilities split out separately) based on independent judgment, but this is a real limitation on how independent the M5 evaluation is. A blind re-author (or a second author) before drawing strong conclusions would strengthen this.

components.name: Application Assembly
components.description: The top-level Starlette object users instantiate; owns configuration, the Router, middleware list, and exception handlers, and lazily builds the full ASGI middleware stack.

components.name: Routing
components.description: Matches an incoming ASGI scope to a handler. Router holds the route table and handles lifespan; Route/WebSocketRoute/Mount/Host implement a common matches/handle/url_path_for interface; compile_path + the Convertor classes turn '{name:type}' path segments into regexes.

components.name: HTTP & WebSocket Connections
components.description: Read-side abstractions over one incoming ASGI connection: Request/HTTPConnection for http scopes, WebSocket for websocket scopes.

components.name: Responses & Background Tasks
components.description: The write side: Response and its concrete subclasses (HTML/plain-text/JSON/redirect/streaming/file), plus BackgroundTask(s) for post-response work.

components.name: Middleware Stack
components.description: The Middleware wrapper plus every concrete ASGI middleware shipped with Starlette (CORS, GZip, HTTPS redirect, trusted host, sessions, WSGI bridge, authentication, request-body limit) and the streaming-to-dispatch adapter BaseHTTPMiddleware.

components.name: Error & Exception Handling
components.description: Maps raised exceptions to responses at two levels: ServerErrorMiddleware (outermost, unhandled 500s) and ExceptionMiddleware (declared handlers), sharing the wrap_app_handling_exceptions machinery; HTTPException/WebSocketException are the exception vocabulary.

components.name: Data Structures
components.description: Immutable/mutable value types used throughout the request/response cycle: URL, Headers, QueryParams, the MultiDict family, FormData, UploadFile, State, Address, Secret.

components.name: Form & Multipart Parsing
components.description: Streaming parsers that turn a request body into FormData: FormParser (urlencoded) and MultiPartParser (multipart/form-data).

components.name: Endpoints, Static Files & Templating
components.description: Optional higher-level building blocks for handlers: class-based HTTPEndpoint/WebSocketEndpoint, StaticFiles for serving a directory, Jinja2Templates for HTML rendering.

components.name: Async Concurrency Utilities
components.description: Small internal helpers for bridging sync/async code and running iterables/callables off the event loop: run_in_threadpool, iterate_in_threadpool, is_async_callable, task-group helpers.

components.name: Optional Services
components.description: Independent opt-in subsystems bundled with Starlette but not on the core request path: environment-based Config, the AuthenticationBackend/requires() authorization layer, OpenAPI SchemaGenerator, and the requests-based TestClient.
